name: auros-web
description: auros.org — static site. Astro, static output, no client framework for content pages (spec §6D).

scripts.//build: Gates in the order that makes a failure cheap to read. `lint` reads the sources and needs no build. `astro check` is types. Then the build. Then `verify:built`, which MUST run last because both of its checks measure the BUILT pages: contrast resolves the real cascade over the real DOM, and the font check reads the characters a browser is actually asked to render.
scripts.//test: src/terrain/terrain.test.ts asserts the §7 properties the terrain module’s own comments say are proved rather than believed: the 18-colour ceiling against the real output buffer, the ore budget, the fixed seed, Math.random being unreachable, and window-crop determinism. It was referenced by no script, no workflow and no line of /verify, and could not be executed at all — its relative imports were extensionless, so `node --experimental-strip-types` could not resolve them. A gate nobody runs is a gate that does not exist. It now runs here, and `build` runs it BEFORE astro build so a broken invariant costs seconds rather than a full build.
scripts.build: pnpm run lint && astro check --minimumSeverity error && pnpm run test && astro build && pnpm run verify:built
scripts.//lighthouse: Spec §6D: Lighthouse ≥ 95 on mobile. Measured against dist/ served by tools/serve-dist.mjs, with the lighthouse pinned in devDependencies. `lighthouse` is one run, for iterating; `lighthouse:ci` is the median of three, which is what the gate reads — never the best of three.
scripts.//nojs: Spec §6D: works with JS disabled down to a mailto fallback. Fetches every built page over HTTP and PARSES it — nothing executes — then asserts the argument survives, no large block waits on a script, and a mailto to the address copy.ts owns is reachable by links that exist in the served bytes.
scripts.//content-js: §6D: no client-side framework for content pages. Signature-matches the built bundles and the inline scripts, refuses a render-blocking <script src>, refuses a <canvas> in the served HTML (§7's terrain is generated after parse so it cannot be laid out before first paint), and holds each page to a committed gzipped JavaScript budget.
scripts.//prove-red: D34/D37. Breaks nine specific things and requires the gate that owns each to go red FOR THE STATED REASON, plus both gates green unmutated. Without this, a Lighthouse gate pointed at an empty directory passes forever.
scripts.verify:built: node tools/contrast.mjs && node tools/fetch-fonts.mjs --verify && node tools/nojs.mjs && node tools/content-js.mjs

//snapshot: Two committed snapshots, both written only from logs fetched from the GitHub Actions API. `snapshot:build-log` re-cuts the LATEST completed run; `snapshot:notable` re-cuts the PINNED set in tools/notable-runs.manifest.json, which is what keeps the console from being whatever today happened to be. Neither can run without a token and neither writes a line it did not fetch. `tools/build-console.test.mjs` runs in `test` and needs no network: it checks what those two committed, and breaks each property on purpose to watch the refusal fire (D34, D37).
